question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
answer:
Before launch, the heaters of oxygen tank No. 2 ran on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The board report called the switch failure a serious oversight. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not state outright that the board named the thermostatic switches as the cause of the fire. They only link the switch failure to the explosion, so I am not claiming more than that.

question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot. [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". His exposure set off the crew swap. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

The swap brought in Jack Swigert as Apollo 13 command module pilot. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Apollo 13 role is prime command module pilot (was backup command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

Swigert later won a seat in the US House of Representatives. He was elected in 1982 but died before taking office. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

The brain does not say what caused his death.

question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
answer:
The tank was Oxygen tank No. 2. Its note says the tank was "carried by [[command-service-module]]" (a link, not a fact line). The command and service module is the spacecraft that carried it. The command-service-module note states "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

The Apollo 11 crew member who piloted that spacecraft was Michael Collins. His note states "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". Its links also say "piloted [[command-service-module]]".

During the landing, Collins stayed in lunar orbit. His note states "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". He did not take part in the descent or touchdown. Armstrong and Aldrin made the landing.

question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?

The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes don't say how the instructions were worded or how long the build took.

question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
